guitar.guitaristsText: Keith Richards / Ronnie Wood / Mick Taylor
guitar.modelsText: Fender Telecaster ('Micawber', 5-string open-G) / Gibson Les Paul / ES series
guitar.evidence: Keith Richards' 5-string open-G-tuned Telecaster 'Micawber' is one of the most famous specific guitars in rock history; this justifies high rather than medium confidence.
guitar.notes: Upgraded confidence from medium to high due to Richards' very specifically documented guitar/tuning setup.

tone.target: wah-driven dirty funk-rock with loose Stones crunch
tone.profile: wah-driven dirty funk-rock with loose Stones crunch
tone.summary: Wah -> Boost/OD -> UK 50 Amp -> UK Vintage 4x12 Cab. Use Chorus sparingly for texture.
gearClues: small British combo or low-gain Marshall

rig.name: The Rolling Stones - Sympathy For The Devil - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide the initial dirty crunch and loose grit required for rhythm playing.
Deliver the pronounced wah signature essential for lead phrases and funk rhythm.
Add extra bite and dirty saturation for the 'Stones crunch' without modern high gain.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated low-gain British amp model, but RAT-style provides the necessary aggressive grit.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the small British combo amp sound, providing classic, loose headroom and grit.
Provide the classic British cabinet tone and necessary punch for the genre.
Add subtle vintage texture for depth without sounding modern or lush.
blocks.gap: The Chorus is used sparingly to add dimension, avoiding the 'lush' sound that was requested to be avoided.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic echo for space and depth without excessive reverb.
blocks.gap: Used as a controlled, non-lush ambience replacement for traditional reverb.

blocks.purpose: Provide minimal, controlled room ambience to keep the tone grounded and dry.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is kept at a very low mix to avoid 'lush' sounds while adding necessary space.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the generic 4x12 IR for a vintage British speaker that better captures the loose, dirty funk-rock tone.

proposals.reason: A smaller vintage cab (1x12/2x12) better matches the small British combo amp sound and provides a tighter, less massive tone for funk-rock.
